loText: Differentiate between through-the-cycle credit rating system and point-in-time credit rating system.
question: A quantitative model validator at a credit rating agency in country WYZ is reviewing models developed by a credit risk analytics group. The validator observes that the rating migration matrix model is based on the data from 2013 to 2022. During these 10 years the economy of country WYZ experienced a mild recession as well as periods of economic growth. However, it is expected that in 2023 a severe downturn greater in magnitude than any previously observed downturn will hit the economy. Which of the following observations would the validator be correct to make?

options.A: The rating migration matrix uses the through-the-cycle approach to managing data and will underestimate the default probabilities for the year 2023.
options.B: The rating migration matrix uses the through-the-cycle approach to managing data and will overestimate the default probabilities for the year 2023.
options.C: The rating migration matrix uses the point-in-time approach to managing data and will underestimate the default probabilities for the year 2023.
options.D: The rating migration matrix uses the point-in-time approach to managing data and will overestimate the default probabilities for the year 2023.

solution:
**Concept**

A through-the-cycle rating or migration matrix averages over a full economic cycle, so it is stable but slow to reflect current conditions. A point-in-time measure reflects the conditions of the moment. An average over good and mildly bad years understates defaults in a severe downturn and overstates them in a boom.

**Exam trap.** Two decisions in one option: the label (through-the-cycle versus point-in-time) and the direction of the error. Settle each separately. The average of mild years is always too optimistic for a severe year.

loText: Evaluate the characteristics of sound Early Warning Indicators (EWI) measures.
question:
A senior risk analyst at a Japanese regional bank is presenting the automobile dashboard analogy for early warning indicators (EWIs) to newly hired analysts. She uses three recent events at the bank:

I. The retail division launched a JPY deposit special to raise rate-sensitive liabilities.

II. The bank’s Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) dropped below a specified internal threshold.

III. Call centre volumes rose dramatically over two days, for reasons not yet known.

Which of the following correctly maps each event to the dashboard light it is analogous to?

options.A: I: turn signal; II: check engine light; III: low oil light
options.B: I: turn signal; II: low oil light; III: check engine light
options.C: I: low oil light; II: turn signal; III: check engine light
options.D: I: check engine light; II: low oil light; III: turn signal

solution:
Dashboard analogy: map a deposit special, an LCR threshold breach and a call-centre spike to the three dashboard lights.

**Concept and theory**

GARP opens the chapter with an analogy: EWIs are like the warning lights on an automobile dashboard. A driver does not read the engine’s internals directly; a small set of lights tells the driver when something needs attention and how urgently. In liquidity risk management (LRM), EWIs play the same role for bank leadership, which is responsible for identifying and managing the underlying liquidity risk factors. GARP uses three lights, and each carries a distinct meaning:

| Light | What it tells the driver | LRM example in GARP |
|---|---|---|
| Turn signal (“blinker”) | An intentional, risky activity: a purposeful change of direction | Running a […]

loText: Evaluate the characteristics of sound Early Warning Indicators (EWI) measures.
question:
An internal auditor at an Australian mutual bank is reviewing the bank’s policy on early warning indicators. The policy contains the following statements:

I. EWIs are changes in key metrics, which may be qualitative or quantitative, and the signals they give can vary in severity and priority.

II. The most important use of an EWI trigger is to initiate management discussions and actions, and these should be formally documented.

III. An EWI signal requires management discussion only once the underlying metric has breached a regulatory minimum, such as an LCR of 100%.

IV. A trigger that simply confirms treasury is aware of a business line’s AUD deposit campaign, so that it can increase its high-quality liquid asset buffer cost-efficiently, is a valid use of an EWI.

Which of the statements are consistent with the reading?

options.A: I and II only
options.B: II and IV only
options.C: I, II and III only
options.D: I, II and IV only

solution:
Internal audit of an EWI policy: nature of EWIs and the main objective of EWI triggers.

**Concept and theory**

An early warning indicator is not a risk measure in the sense of a number that captures how much could be lost. It is a change in a key metric that could signal a pending liquidity problem. Schweser stresses two features of that definition. First, EWIs can be qualitative or quantitative: GARP’s examples range from the LCR (a ratio) to negative publicity and call centre volumes (much softer signals), and the BCBS list it reproduces explicitly contains both kinds. Second, EWI signals vary in severity and priority, which is why the dashboard analogy uses different lights.

loText: Evaluate the characteristics of sound Early Warning Indicators (EWI) measures.
question: A supervisor at a U.K. regulator is reviewing the draft EWI measures of a GBP 40 billion retail bank. The draft contains only: the month-end LCR as reported, the month-end loan-to-deposit ratio, and month-end deposit balances by product. All three are calculated under business-as-usual conditions, and the bank has GBP 6 billion of undrawn committed credit facilities to corporate clients. Which feedback is most consistent with the hallmarks of sound EWI measures set out in BCBS Principle 5?

options.A: Add metrics that project cash flows and future liquidity positions, take account of off-balance sheet risks such as the committed facilities, and cover stressed as well as normal conditions over several horizons.
options.B: Replace the balance sheet structure metrics with projected cash flow metrics, because Principle 5 treats the structure of the balance sheet as backward looking and outside the scope of EWIs.
options.C: Add metrics derived only from external market prices, because Principle 5 defines a forward-looking metric as one that is implied by market prices rather than by the bank’s own data.
options.D: Add the off-balance sheet committed facilities, but keep a single month-end horizon for every measure, because a common horizon keeps the measures comparable across the balance sheet.

solution:
Supervisory feedback on a month-end, business-as-usual EWI draft against BCBS Principle 5.

**Concept and theory**

Within the M.E.R.I.T. framework, “M” (measures) is the first building block. GARP grounds the hallmarks of sound measures in Principle 5 of the BCBS “Sound Principles” (2008). The principle says that, to obtain a forward-looking view of liquidity risk exposures, a bank should use metrics that assess:

(a) the structure of the balance sheet, as well as metrics that

(b) project cash flows and future liquidity positions, taking into account

(c) off-balance sheet risks.

question:
A treasury analyst at a Singapore bank compares two candidate EWIs: total deposit balances, and deposit balances of the more volatile segments (high-net-worth and rate-sensitive). Over the past week the bank’s LCR was 142% and its senior CDS spread was unchanged. Deposit balances moved as follows:

| Segment | Start of week (SGD m) | End of week (SGD m) |
|---|---|---|
| Insured retail current accounts | 18,400 | 18,950 |
| Corporate operating accounts | 9,600 | 9,780 |
| High-net-worth deposits | 4,200 | 3,570 |
| Rate-sensitive online term deposits | 2,800 | 2,380 |

Which of the following best evaluates the two candidate EWIs?

options.A: The total-deposit EWI is acceptable, but the segment EWI is sharper: about 15% of volatile balances left while total deposits fell by less than 1%.
options.B: The total-deposit EWI is sharper, since offsetting inflows cancel noise across segments, and its fall of less than 1% needs no further attention.
options.C: The segment EWI is sharper because sharpness means greater statistical accuracy: about 15% of volatile balances left while total deposits fell by less than 1%.
options.D: The segment EWI is sharper: about 15% of volatile balances left, while total deposits fell by about 3.0%, so the aggregate signal is only modestly weaker.

solution:
Total deposits versus volatile-segment deposits as EWIs: which is sharper and what the data show.

**Concept and theory**

GARP asks for EWIs that are forward looking and sharp. Sharpness is the granularity and specificity of an indicator as it pertains to the institution’s profile. A sharp indicator is a signal that does not go unnoticed within the mass of data. The deposit example is GARP’s own: detecting a drop in overall deposit balances is an acceptable EWI, but detecting drops in the balances of more volatile segments, such as high-net-worth customers or rate-sensitive products, brings into focus that certain important classes of customers are leaving the bank.

loText: Evaluate the characteristics of sound Early Warning Indicators (EWI) measures.
question: A senior risk analyst at a Canadian bank is reviewing a proposal to use government-reported quarterly GDP growth as the main EWI of a deterioration in the general economy, which drives credit losses and deposit behaviour on the bank’s CAD 85 billion balance sheet. Which recommendation is most consistent with the reading?

options.A: Retain reported GDP as the primary signal, because a published figure that confirms a downturn has occurred is the most reliable basis for a warning.
options.B: Treat reported GDP as a lagging indicator, and develop proxies for the performance of the general economy from internal loan portfolio metrics.
options.C: Replace reported GDP with the bank’s realised credit loss rate for the last fiscal year, because internal data are by definition leading indicators.
options.D: Retain reported GDP but break it down by province, because making an indicator more granular converts a lagging indicator into a leading one.

solution:
Replacing reported GDP with leading proxies built from internal loan portfolio metrics.

**Concept and theory**

The first quality GARP asks of EWI measures is that they be leading, that is forward looking. A leading indicator provides information and signals potential stress prior to the occurrence of an actual event. A lagging indicator reports on events that have already occurred. GARP’s example of a lagging indicator is government-reported GDP: by the time a quarter’s GDP is published, the economic slowdown it measures has already happened, and the bank’s borrowers and depositors have already been affected.

loText: Evaluate the characteristics of sound Early Warning Indicators (EWI) measures.
question: The CRO of a Chinese joint-stock bank wants the bank’s EWI suite to capture emerging, internally driven stress events before they become public knowledge. The bank funds a CNY 1.2 trillion balance sheet largely with corporate and interbank deposits. Which proposal best achieves this objective?

options.A: Rely chiefly on the bank’s own CDS spread and share price, since market prices react to bank-specific problems before management is aware of them internally.
options.B: Rely chiefly on external measures such as sovereign spreads and interbank rates, since internally driven stress always appears first as a market-wide dislocation.
options.C: Rely chiefly on rating agency actions on the bank, since a downgrade is the earliest confirmation that internally driven stress has emerged.
options.D: Monitor internal data such as loan performance, planned significant accounting adjustments and operational losses, which can reveal stress before outsiders see it.

solution:
Capturing internally driven stress before it becomes public knowledge.

**Concept and theory**

Internal and external measures are not just two lists; they play different roles in timing. GARP says EWIs should be positioned to capture emerging internally driven stress events before they become public knowledge, and gives three examples of how: monitoring loan performance, planned significant accounting adjustments, and operational losses. Schweser puts it as: an effective EWI should be able to identify signs of internal stress before these issues become visible to external parties.

loText: Evaluate the characteristics of sound Early Warning Indicators (EWI) measures.
question: A member of the board risk committee at a eurozone savings bank is reviewing how the bank’s EWIs are used across operating environments. The bank holds a EUR 3.5 billion liquidity buffer. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

options.A: EWI metrics need to be tracked only once stress emerges, because in business-as-usual conditions their movements reflect noise rather than weaknesses in the balance sheet.
options.B: Stressed measures and limits should be kept out of the EWI list and reported only within the stress testing programme, so that hypothetical and actual values are never mixed.
options.C: Tracking EWIs in business-as-usual conditions alerts leadership to emerging weaknesses, while including stressed measures and limits gauges whether the liquidity buffer is adequate under stress.
options.D: Stress testing results can confirm concentrations that the bank has already identified, but they cannot expose concentrations or risks that were previously unidentified.

solution:
Use of EWIs in business-as-usual and in stressed environments.

**Concept and theory**

GARP’s section “Environments, Both Normal and Stressed” gives EWIs a role in both states, for different reasons.

Business-as-usual (normal) environment. EWIs are meant to give a heads-up for an upcoming potential disaster, so tracking them only once stress has arrived defeats their purpose. Tracking appropriate EWI metrics in a business-as-usual environment is essential, because any deterioration in them alerts leadership either to weaknesses in the bank’s balance sheet or to challenging circumstances emerging in the markets where it operates. Schweser: EWIs should be used in normal operating states to warn of any potential future worsening of the bank’s financial position.

question:
An internal auditor at a U.S. bank is reviewing the update cycles of four EWIs in the bank’s USD liquidity dashboard. The bank’s assets and liabilities have a range of maturities, and it has a modest trading book.

| Indicator | Update cycle |
|---|---|
| Wholesale funding rollover rate | Daily |
| Outflows from rate-sensitive deposit segments | Weekly |
| Share of funding from the ten largest providers | Monthly |
| Commercial real estate loan delinquency rate | Quarterly |

Which evaluation of the update cycles is most accurate?

options.A: All four cycles are adequate, because an EWI needs to be refreshed only as often as the bank’s quarterly regulatory returns are filed.
options.B: Only the daily cycle is adequate, because weekly and monthly cycles are too slow and every EWI must be monitored on an intraday basis.
options.C: The quarterly cycle is the most appropriate, because a long horizon matches the duration of the loan book while the daily cycle mainly adds noise.
options.D: The quarterly cycle is unlikely to satisfy the “early” aspect of an EWI, while daily, weekly and monthly cycles match typical forecasting and operating cycles.

solution:
Auditing update cycles of four EWIs: which satisfy the “early” aspect.

**Concept and theory**

GARP’s subsection “Spanning Various Time Horizons” makes two points. First, EWI coverage cannot be static: it must reflect various time horizons, to match the institution’s unique balance sheet needs and the market and economic conditions under which it operates. Schweser gives the reason: a bank has assets and liabilities of differing durations, so a single horizon cannot capture every vulnerability. Second, there is a practical ceiling on how slow an EWI can be. Typical cycle time horizons, matching banking forecasts and business operations, tend to be daily, weekly or monthly. loText: Evaluate the characteristics of sound Early Warning Indicators (EWI) measures.
question: A risk consultant is reviewing the EWI framework of a U.S. regional bank. The bank has built a well-designed suite of leading, granular, internal and external measures, calculated daily from an integrated USD data warehouse. However, threshold breaches are only recorded in a log that is reviewed at the annual model validation, and no manager is assigned to act on them. Which evaluation is most accurate?

options.A: The measures may be sound, but unless the framework is linked to escalation processes it is a mere academic exercise with no favourable effect on liquidity risk management.
options.B: The framework is robust, because an appropriate set of measures is the first essential building block and a well-designed set of measures is sufficient by itself.
options.C: The weakness lies in the measures: leading and granular indicators generate too many signals to act on, so the bank should move to lagging indicators instead.
options.D: The framework is robust, because the integrated data warehouse already ensures that reported metrics are accurate and in sync, which removes the need for escalation.

A well-designed set of measures with no escalation link: evaluating the framework.

**Concept and theory**

GARP summarises the EWI framework as M.E.R.I.T.: Measures, Escalation, Reporting, Integrated systems and Thresholds. The components are not a menu; they form a chain. GARP’s key sentence is that, while an appropriate set of measures is the first essential building block for a robust EWI framework, it will be a “mere academic exercise” if the framework is not eventually linked to escalation processes. The journey from measures to escalation is facilitated by timely reporting, supported by integrated systems and data and by relevant, properly calibrated thresholds. loText: Identify EWI guidelines from banking regulators and supervisors (OCC, BCBS, Federal Reserve).
question:
A member of the risk committee at a mid-sized U.S. regional bank is reviewing a one-page appendix to the bank’s EWI policy. The appendix summarises the four supervisory guidelines that the policy cites as core guiding principles for EWI selection and monitoring:

I. OCC (2012), drawn from the Liquidity booklet of the Comptroller’s Handbook, asks for EWIs that signal whether embedded triggers in products such as callable public debt and OTC derivatives transactions are about to be breached.

II. BCBS (2008), the Sound Principles, is the source of the intraday liquidity monitoring indicators, such as daily maximum liquidity and intraday throughput.

III. SR 10-6, the 2010 Interagency Policy Statement on Funding and Liquidity Risk Management, asks management to use EWIs and event triggers tailored to the institution’s specific liquidity risk profile.

IV. Widening debt or credit default swap spreads appear as an EWI only in the OCC (2012) guideline and in none of the other guidelines summarised.

loText: Identify EWI guidelines from banking regulators and supervisors (OCC, BCBS, Federal Reserve).
question:
A treasurer at a Japanese regional bank is updating the bank’s liquidity EWI list. The bank’s balance sheet includes the following items:

| Item | Amount (JPY bn) | Feature |
|---|---|---|
| Callable senior public bond issued | 40 | Call option embedded in the bond |
| OTC interest rate swaps under CSA | 25 | Rating-downgrade collateral trigger |
| Retail time deposits | 310 | No embedded feature |

The treasurer wants to cite the supervisory guideline that specifically calls for EWIs covering the first two items. Which of the following best identifies that guideline and what its EWIs should signal?

options.A: OCC (2012): EWIs that signal whether the embedded triggers are about to be breached, or whether contingent risks are likely to materialize.
options.B: BCBS (2008): EWIs that signal whether the embedded triggers are about to be breached, or whether contingent risks are likely to materialize.
options.C: OCC (2012): EWIs that confirm the embedded triggers have already been breached, so that the resulting contingent liabilities can be recorded.
options.D: BCBS (2012): intraday indicators that track the time-specific payments that arise once the embedded triggers have been exercised.

solution:
Treasurer of a Japanese bank with callable public debt and OTC swaps with downgrade triggers cites the right guideline.

Some liquidity risks are not visible in today’s cash flows because they sit inside contracts as options or triggers. A callable public bond, or an OTC derivative under a credit support annex with a rating-downgrade trigger, can turn a quiet balance sheet item into a sudden cash demand when a condition is met: collateral must be posted, or funding must be replaced. loText: Identify EWI guidelines from banking regulators and supervisors (OCC, BCBS, Federal Reserve).
question: A treasury analyst at a London clearing bank that settles large GBP payment volumes is building an intraday liquidity dashboard. Her manager asks her to use only indicators drawn from the BCBS (2012) intraday liquidity monitoring guideline. Which of the following indicators is least likely to be drawn from that guideline?

options.A: Intraday credit lines extended to financial institution customers.
options.B: Timing of intraday payments.
options.C: Increased concerns over the funding of off-balance-sheet items.
options.D: Time-specific and other critical obligations.

solution:
London clearing bank’s intraday dashboard: which indicator does not come from BCBS (2012)?

**Concept and theory**

Most EWIs look at days, weeks or months. A bank that settles large payment flows can still fail within a single day: it may be solvent and liquid at the close but unable to make a time-critical payment at 11:00 because the incoming payments it relies on have not arrived. The BCBS addressed this in 2012 with “Monitoring Indicators for Intraday Liquidity”. In GARP’s Table 3.2, the BCBS-2012 column lists intraday liquidity monitoring indicators:

| Indicator | What it captures |
|---|---|
| Daily maximum liquidity (requirement) | Peak intraday liquidity the bank needs |
| Available intraday liquidity | Resources it can use within the day |
| Total payments | Gross payment flows  […]

loText: Identify EWI guidelines from banking regulators and supervisors (OCC, BCBS, Federal Reserve).
question:
The CRO of a Chinese bank active in CNY large-value payment systems is reviewing a junior analyst’s summary of the BCBS (2012) guideline on intraday liquidity monitoring indicators. The summary states that the indicators include:

I. Daily maximum liquidity and available intraday liquidity.

II. The value of customer payments made on behalf of financial institution customers, and intraday credit lines extended to financial institution customers.

III. A decrease in the weighted average maturity of liabilities and increases in currency mismatches.

IV. The timing of intraday payments and intraday throughput.

Which parts of the summary are accurate?

options.A: I and II only
options.B: I, II, and IV only
options.C: II and III only
options.D: I, II, III, and IV

solution:
CRO of a Chinese bank audits a junior analyst’s summary of the BCBS (2012) intraday indicators.

**Concept and theory**

BCBS (2012) gives supervisors and banks a common vocabulary for intraday liquidity. The logic follows the stages of a payment day:

(i) Need: how much liquidity the bank requires at the worst point of the day (daily maximum liquidity).

(ii) Resources: how much it can draw on within the day (available intraday liquidity).

(iii) Flows: total payments, the timing of intraday payments, and intraday throughput (how much of the day’s payments have settled by given times).

(iv) Obligations: time-specific and other critical obligations that cannot slip.

loText: Identify EWI guidelines from banking regulators and supervisors (OCC, BCBS, Federal Reserve).
question: A Federal Reserve examiner is reviewing the liquidity policy of a U.S. bank holding company with USD 85 billion of assets against SR 10-6, the 2010 Interagency Policy Statement on Funding and Liquidity Risk Management. Which of the following best describes the EWI guidance in SR 10-6?

options.A: Management should monitor for potential liquidity stress events using EWIs and event triggers tailored to its specific liquidity risk profile; early recognition supports progressive states of readiness and communication inside and outside the institution.
options.B: Management should monitor for potential liquidity stress events using a common set of EWIs and event triggers prescribed for all institutions; early recognition lets supervisors compare readiness across institutions and communicate with outside parties.
options.C: Management should monitor for potential liquidity stress events using EWIs and event triggers tailored to its specific liquidity risk profile; early signals should be communicated only within the institution until the event has materialized.
options.D: Management should monitor for potential liquidity stress events using EWIs that signal whether embedded triggers in callable public debt and OTC derivatives are about to be breached, as the core requirement of the statement.

solution:
Federal Reserve examiner checks a U.S. BHC’s policy against the EWI guidance in SR 10-6.

**Concept and theory**

SR 10-6 is the Federal Reserve’s issuance of the 2010 Interagency Policy Statement on Funding and Liquidity Risk Management, an interagency statement. Its EWI guidance in GARP’s Table 3.2 has four elements:

(i) Tools: institution management should monitor for potential liquidity stress events using early-warning indicators and event triggers.

(ii) Tailoring: the institution should tailor these indicators to its specific liquidity risk profile. Schweser says the EWIs should be consistent with the firm’s liquidity risk profile.

(iii) Readiness: early recognition of potential events lets the institution position itself into progressive states of readiness as the event evolves.

loText: Identify EWI guidelines from banking regulators and supervisors (OCC, BCBS, Federal Reserve).
question: The head of liquidity risk at a German bank with EUR 210 billion of assets is drafting the regulatory citations for the bank’s EWI framework. Which of the following attributions is most accurate?

options.A: FRB SR 12-7 states that, for a forward-looking view of liquidity risk, a bank should use metrics that assess balance sheet structure, project cash flows, and take account of off-balance sheet risks.
options.B: BCBS Principle 5 states that the liquidity risk management framework should be end-to-end and should sufficiently capture the banking organization’s exposures, activities, and risks.
options.C: BCBS Principle 5 calls for metrics on balance sheet structure, projected cash flows and future liquidity positions, and off-balance sheet risks, across both normal and stressed conditions.
options.D: BCBS Principle 5 calls for metrics on balance sheet structure, projected cash flows and future liquidity positions, and off-balance sheet risks, under business-as-usual conditions only.

solution:
Head of liquidity risk at a German bank attributes two further regulatory statements cited in GARP’s EWI chapter.

It states that to obtain a forward-looking view of liquidity risk exposures, a bank should use metrics that assess (a) the structure of the balance sheet, and metrics that (b) project cash flows and future liquidity positions, taking into account

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question:
A member of the board risk committee at a Canadian bank is reviewing a draft policy that describes how the bank’s early warning indicators (EWIs) will be used within its CAD liquidity risk management framework. The draft contains the following statements:

I. The EWIs will have a tangible and favourable effect on liquidity risk governance only when they are linked to a clearly defined escalation plan.

II. The governance overseeing the escalation of EWI-triggered actions will be formalised and documented as part of the liquidity risk management framework and included in the contingency funding plan.

III. Because escalation criteria for EWIs are prescribed uniformly by banking supervisors, the bank will adopt the supervisory escalation criteria without modification.

IV. Because a sound set of measures is the first essential building block of the EWI framework, the measures deliver most of the framework’s value even before they are linked to escalation processes.

Which of the statements are accurate?

options.A: I only
options.B: I and III only
options.C: I and II only
options.D: I, II, and IV only

solution:
Canadian bank board policy review: which statements about EWIs and escalation are accurate.

**Concept and theory**

GARP summarises the EWI framework with the acronym M.E.R.I.T.: Measures, Escalation, Reporting, Integrated systems, and Thresholds. The five components play different roles. Measures are the raw material: the indicators themselves, internal and external, leading and sharp. GARP calls an appropriate set of measures the first essential building block. It then warns that the framework becomes a “mere academic exercise” if it is not eventually linked to escalation processes. The other three components (timely reporting, integrated systems and data, and properly calibrated thresholds) are what make the move from measures to escalation possible.

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question: The treasurer of a Japanese bank receives an EWI alert: projected drawdowns on committed credit facilities extended to corporate clients signal a potentially large JPY cash outflow over the next month. The bank is not in a crisis: its funding markets remain open, its rating is unchanged, and other EWIs are within normal bounds. The bank’s liquid asset buffer currently stands at JPY 1.4 trillion. Which of the following responses is most consistent with an effective EWI escalation policy?

options.A: The treasurer authorises a check on future asset growth directly, since all responses to EWI signals fall within the delegation of the corporate treasurer.
options.B: The signal is escalated to the asset-liability committee (ALCO), which may authorise a check on future asset growth.
options.C: Management initiates the contingency funding plan at once, since every EWI that signals a cash outflow requires the plan to be activated.
options.D: No escalation takes place until the outflow causes a regulatory limit to be breached, since the role of EWIs is to record breaches once they occur.

solution:
Japanese bank: an EWI signals a potentially large cash outflow outside a crisis; who responds and how.

**Concept and theory**

Escalation answers a practical question: once an EWI fires, who acts, and with what tool? GARP’s starting point is that escalation criteria are bespoke to each bank. Whatever the criteria, an effective policy sends limit breaches to the level of management that has the authority to undertake the corrective action. GARP then gives three tiers, scaled to severity:

| Severity of signal | Who acts | Typical response |
|---|---|---|
| Modest | Corporate treasurer (own delegation) | Increase the liquid asset buffer |
| Potentially large cash outflow | ALCO | Authorise a check on future asset growth |
| Most extreme cases | Management | Initiate the contingency funding  […]

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question: An internal auditor at a London broker-dealer with a significant trading focus is reviewing an incident. At 10:40 a.m. on a volatile day, initial margin calls on the firm’s cleared derivatives rose by GBP 640 million. The firm’s EWI dashboard is compiled once a day after the close, so treasury first saw the signal the following morning. The firm’s most recent reported LCR was 148%. Which of the following recommendations best describes good practice for EWI reporting at this firm?

options.A: Keep daily reporting: it is common practice, and intraday reporting is mainly adopted by retail-funded banks whose deposit balances can move within hours.
options.B: Move every indicator on the dashboard to intraday reporting, since supervisors require intraday reporting of all EWIs at firms with trading activity.
options.C: Keep daily reporting: any indicator that is refreshed at least once a month already satisfies the “early” aspect of an early warning indicator.
options.D: Daily reporting is common practice, but a firm with a significant trading focus should move toward intraday reporting of certain measures, given its greater exposure to external market conditions.

solution:
London broker-dealer: margin calls spike intraday but the EWI dashboard is compiled once daily.

**Concept and theory**

Reporting is the R in M.E.R.I.T. An early warning indicator is only early if management sees it in time. GARP states the purpose directly: EWI reporting must be timely so that management has enough lead time to adjust before a potential crisis. It then describes industry practice in three steps:

- **Daily is the common baseline.** It is common practice to report the EWI dashboard daily, and most institutions do some daily liquidity reporting.
- **Leaders go further.** Leading institutions are moving toward intraday reporting of certain measures, not of every indicator.

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question: The CRO of an Australian bank is redesigning the daily EWI pack sent to senior management. The current pack runs to 14 pages and contains 160 indicators, and executives say they cannot tell which signals matter. The bank’s AUD wholesale funding totals AUD 38 billion. Which of the following design principles is most consistent with sound EWI reporting?

options.A: The pack should be broad enough to give wide coverage of the bank’s liquidity risks, yet specific enough to communicate only the key messages.
options.B: The pack should maximise coverage by giving every indicator equal prominence, since any filtering of the pack risks hiding a warning signal.
options.C: The pack should report only the indicators that have turned red, since indicators showing green or amber need no attention from management.
options.D: The pack should be limited to externally observable market indicators, since internal indicators cannot be calculated and reported consistently.

solution:
Australian bank: redesigning a 160-indicator daily EWI pack that executives cannot read.

**Concept and theory**

Timeliness is not the only requirement for EWI reporting. A report that arrives on time but buries the signal fails just as badly as one that arrives late. GARP therefore adds a design requirement: reporting must strike a balance between being (a) broad enough to provide wide coverage, and (b) specific enough to communicate only the key messages. Schweser puts it the same way: broad enough to cover the full range of relevant matters, but focused enough to cover what is most important.

The two failure modes mirror each other.

| Design error | What happens | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Too narrow | Some risk sources are not covered | A threat builds up unseen |

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question: A risk consultant is reviewing the EWI framework of a Brazilian bank. The bank’s liquidity stress test takes retail deposit volumes from a month-end general ledger extract that is adjusted by hand, while its EWI for week-over-week declines in deposit funding uses a daily feed from the core banking system. At the last month-end the two deposit figures differed by BRL 2.4 billion. The bank plans to add 35 internal indicators, such as loan performance and operational losses, to its EWI list. Which of the following recommendations is most consistent with sound practice for integrated systems?

options.A: Replace the internal deposit EWI with market-based indicators such as the bank’s CDS spread, since market data avoid internal reconciliation problems.
options.B: Accept the difference, since stressed and non-stressed measures should be drawn from separate data sources to keep the stress test independent.
options.C: Derive the deposit volumes feeding the stress test from the same source system used for the week-over-week deposit EWI, so that the reported metrics are accurate and in sync.
options.D: Integrate the data systems first, after which the EWIs will reliably predict any liquidity crisis and the separate stress test can be retired.

solution:
Brazilian bank: stress test and deposit EWI use different source systems that disagree by BRL 2.4 billion.

**Concept and theory**

Integrated systems are the I in M.E.R.I.T. GARP’s starting point is that metrics and reporting are feasible and meaningful only when they are backed by the bank’s ability to calculate the selected metrics and report them consistently. Integrated data and systems give liquidity managers two assurances about every reported metric: it is (a) accurate, and (b) in sync with the other metrics.

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question:
A senior risk analyst at a Singapore bank is reviewing the green-to-amber boundaries of two EWIs over the past 24 months. Both thresholds were calibrated on three years of SGD data.

| EWI | Times amber | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| X: share of funding from overnight interbank borrowing | 46 | 1 investigation found a real issue |
| Y: share of deposits from the top 10 depositors | 0 | rose from 18% to 31% in the period |

Which of the following best describes the calibration of the two EWIs?

options.A: X’s boundary is too narrow, risking a “boy who cried wolf” effect that desensitises management; Y’s boundary is too wide, so its movements go undetected.
options.B: X’s boundary is too wide, so its movements go undetected; Y’s boundary is too narrow, risking a “boy who cried wolf” effect that desensitises management.
options.C: X’s boundary is well calibrated, because frequent amber signals ensure no emerging issue is missed; Y’s boundary is too wide, so its movements go undetected.
options.D: X’s boundary is too narrow, risking a “boy who cried wolf” effect that desensitises management; Y’s boundary is well calibrated, since it confirms a healthy environment.

solution:
Singapore bank: one EWI turns amber 46 times with one real issue; another never leaves green while concentration rises.

**Concept and theory**

Most firms present EWIs with a stoplight. Green means the measure is within normal bounds. Amber means it should be investigated further. Red signals significant concern and may warrant an immediate response. GARP’s calibration discussion focuses on the boundary between green and amber, where the first warning is given.

GARP describes two opposite ways to get this boundary wrong.

| Boundary | Symptom | Consequence |

| Too wide | Metric almost never leaves green | Movements go undetected; the dashboard keeps saying all is well |

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question:
A junior risk analyst at a German savings bank is calibrating thresholds for an EWI that tracks the weekly percentage change in EUR retail deposits. Bank policy sets the amber threshold at 1.5 standard deviations below the historical mean and the red threshold at 2.5 standard deviations below the mean. Four candidate calibration windows are available:

| Window | Period covered | Mean (%) | Std dev (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Last 8 months to last week; no stress episode | −0.10 | 0.60 |
| W2 | 5 years ending 2 years ago; includes a stress episode | −0.30 | 1.90 |
| W3 | Last 4 years to last week; includes a stress episode | −0.20 | 1.20 |
| W4 | Last 2 years to last week; no stress episode | −0.15 | 0.80 |

This week’s change is −2.60%. The bank’s current LCR is 141%. Using the most appropriate window, which of the following statements holds?

options.A: W1: amber at −1.00%, red at −1.60%; the EWI is red.
options.B: W2: amber at −3.15%, red at −5.05%; the EWI is green.
options.C: W4: amber at −1.35%, red at −2.15%; the EWI is red.
options.D: W3: amber at −2.00%, red at −3.20%; the EWI is amber.

solution:
German savings bank: choose the calibration window, compute amber and red thresholds, classify a −2.60% reading.

**Concept and theory**

A threshold has to be anchored in how the indicator normally behaves, and GARP says historical data analysis is commonly used to estimate an EWI’s volatility and calibrate its thresholds. Schweser specifies that past data are used to compute the EWI’s standard deviation. Neither source prescribes a formula for the threshold itself, so the multiples used here (1.5 and 2.5 standard deviations) are bank policy given in the stem.

The source’s guidance is about which data to use. GARP sets three conditions on the calibration series:

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question:
A banking regulator is reviewing the EWI log of a Chinese commercial bank, which uses a green, amber, and red stoplight system. Four entries from the CNY liquidity dashboard log read as follows:

I. Depositor concentration EWI moved to amber; the measure was referred to treasury for further investigation, with no remedial action yet taken.

II. Several EWIs turned red after a two-notch rating downgrade and a sustained run on wholesale funding; management initiated the contingency funding plan.

III. An EWI turned red, signalling a potentially large cash outflow; the treasurer handled it within his own delegation through a modest buffer increase, and ALCO was not informed.

IV. A funding concentration EWI moved from green to amber; management initiated the contingency funding plan immediately, as an amber status calls for an immediate response.

Which of the log entries are consistent with sound use of EWI thresholds and escalation?

options.A: I only
options.B: I and II only
options.C: I, II, and III only
options.D: I, II, and IV only

solution:
Chinese bank EWI log: which recorded responses fit the stoplight status and escalation tiers.

**Concept and theory**

Thresholds and escalation work together. The threshold tells management how serious a signal is, and escalation tells it who acts and how. GARP’s stoplight definitions are:

| Status | GARP meaning | Fitting response |
|---|---|---|
| Green | Within normal bounds | No further action |
| Amber | Should be investigated further | Investigate and follow up |
| Red | Significant concern; may warrant immediate response | Escalate to the authority that fits the severity |

Schweser’s wording is close: green needs no further action, amber needs additional follow-up, and red needs immediate attention to remedy a serious problem.

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question: A treasury analyst at a US bank is reviewing the calibration of the bank’s EWI thresholds, including an EWI on the effective federal funds rate. The bank currently calibrates every threshold from the historical volatility of the indicator. Which of the following statements about threshold calibration is NOT accurate?

options.A: Historical data analysis is commonly used to estimate the volatility of an EWI and calibrate its thresholds, with a series of at least one year used when available.
options.B: Thresholds should be subjected to back-testing to determine whether recalibration is needed.
options.C: Because thresholds calibrated on historical volatility are objective, they should not be overridden by management, even when the FOMC specifies a target range for the rate.
options.D: If possible, the calibration series should include a period of stress, such as 2007-08, to assess more accurately how the metric performs under stressed conditions.

solution:
US bank: which statement about calibrating thresholds, including an EWI on the fed funds rate, is NOT accurate.

**Concept and theory**

Calibration is not a one-off statistical exercise. GARP describes it as a cycle with three parts.

(i) **Historical estimation.** Historical data are commonly used to estimate an EWI’s volatility and calibrate its thresholds. The series should be long enough to be significant, capture recent events and, if possible, include a period of stress such as 2007-08. When available, at least one year of data is used.

(ii) **Back-testing.** The threshold should be subjected to back-testing to determine whether recalibration is needed.

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question: The chief compliance officer of a Spanish bank is presenting to newly hired analysts on how EUR-reporting banks have developed their EWI dashboards since the 2007-08 crisis. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

options.A: The increased attention and resources devoted to EWI dashboards and their governance are largely attributable to supervisory demands such as matters requiring attention and exams, with some credit also due to leadership-initiated projects.
options.B: The increased attention and resources devoted to EWI dashboards and their governance are largely attributable to leadership-initiated projects, with supervisory demands such as matters requiring attention and exams playing a minor role.
options.C: The increased attention and resources devoted to EWI dashboards and their governance are largely attributable to a standard EWI list mandated by the BCBS, which has made dashboards uniform across banks.
options.D: The increased attention and resources devoted to EWI dashboards and their governance are largely attributable to credit rating agencies, which require an EWI dashboard as a condition of assigning a rating.

solution:
Spanish bank briefing: what drove the growth of EWI dashboards and their governance.

**Concept and theory**

GARP’s “Industry Practices” section describes how EWIs have developed in practice. Over recent years banks have increased the attention and resources they devote to developing and maintaining EWI dashboards and the governance around them. GARP gives two drivers, in a clear order of importance:

1. **Mainly supervisory demands.** The extra emphasis is “largely attributed” to supervisory demands, in the form of matters requiring attention (MRAs), examinations, and similar actions.
2. **Partly leadership initiative.** In some cases credit should also go to bank leadership, which launched projects on its own initiative to strengthen liquidity management and risk reporting.

loText: Discuss the applications of EWIs in the context of the liquidity risk management process.
question:
A senior risk analyst at a US regional bank is preparing a report on where EWIs sit within the bank’s USD liquidity risk management process. The draft includes the following statements:

I. A comprehensive framework begins by identifying the liquidity and funding risks inherent in the bank’s business activities; these are recorded in a liquidity risk inventory and assessed before stress tests, EWIs, and a limit and response framework are developed.

II. EWIs should be kept aligned with other core aspects of the framework, such as the risk inventory, stress testing assumptions, cash flow actuals and projections, business plans, and the contingency funding plan.

III. Because idiosyncratic EWIs are tailored to a single bank’s vulnerabilities, supervisors are expected to scrutinise them less closely than market-wide indicators.

IV. Using EWIs to build liquidity buffers ahead of stress can extend the survival horizon cost-effectively, and a strong position in stress can open opportunities such as gains in market share.

Which of the statements should the analyst retain?

options.A: I and II only
options.B: I, II, and III only
options.C: II and IV only
options.D: I, II, and IV only

solution:
US regional bank report: where EWIs sit in the LRM process; which statements to retain.

**Concept and theory**

The LO asks how EWIs are applied in the context of the LRM process, so it helps to see the whole process. GARP describes it as a sequence:

1. **Identify** the liquidity and funding risks inherent in the institution’s business activities.
2. **Record** them in the firm’s liquidity risk inventory.
3. **Assess** them, in a process that involves the businesses, corporate treasury, independent risk management, and other stakeholders.
4. **Measure and monitor** them through a framework of stress tests, EWIs, and a limit and response framework.

loText: Evaluate the characteristics of sound Early Warning Indicators (EWI) measures.
question:
Joe Hart, a market analyst at Smart Investment Bank, has been tasked with the development of early warning signals to help the bank to monitor potential liquidity stress events. At the preliminary stage, Mr. Hart has researched a set of background guidelines as follows:

I. All EWIs must be updated every two months to detect potentially threatening events.

II. The bank should conduct a variety of short-term and protracted bank-specific and market-wide liquidity stress tests using conservative and regularly reviewed assumptions.

III. The bank should establish a robust escalation policy so that critical decisions and transactions are handled at an appropriate level of management.

As a risk analyst, which of the above proposals would you disagree with?

options.A: I
options.B: II
options.C: III
options.D: None of the above

solution:
**Concept**

Early warning indicators must be early: measured frequently (daily, weekly or at most monthly), forward-looking, tied to thresholds and linked to an escalation process and to the contingency funding plan. Supervisory guidance also expects a range of bank-specific and market-wide stress tests and a clear escalation policy.

**Exam trap.** The question asks which proposal to disagree with. The flaw is one number: two months.

loText: Identify EWI guidelines from banking regulators and supervisors (OCC, BCBS, Federal Reserve).
question: The Basel Committee recommends that banks use a set of early warning indicators to identify emerging risks and potential vulnerabilities in their liquidity position. Which of the following is an early warning indicator of a potential liquidity problem?

options.A: Credit rating upgrade
options.B: Increased asset diversification
options.C: Rapid growth in the leverage ratio with significant dependence on short-term repo financing
options.D: Decreased collateral haircuts applied to the bank’s collateralized exposures

solution:
**Concept**

Supervisory lists of early warning indicators include rapid asset growth funded by volatile liabilities, growing concentrations, a shortening of liability maturities, rating downgrades, widening spreads, rising haircuts and collateral calls.

**Exam trap.** Three options are good news with a plausible-sounding label. Check the direction of each change.

loText: Identify EWI guidelines from banking regulators and supervisors (OCC, BCBS, Federal Reserve).
question:
Your Chief Risk Officer asks you to come up with a list of early warning signs for liquidity problems for your bank. Which of the following are early warning indicators of a potential liquidity problem?

I. Narrowing credit default swap spreads

II. Increasing redemptions of CDs prior to maturity

III. Growing concentrations in liabilities

IV. An increase of the weighted average maturity of liabilities

V. Request for additional collateral by counterparties

options.A: (I) and (II)
options.B: (II), (III), and (V)
options.C: (II), (III), (IV), and (V)
options.D: All of the above

solution:
**Concept**

Supervisory lists of early warning indicators of a liquidity problem include: widening credit or CDS spreads, rising funding costs, early redemption of CDs, growing concentrations in assets or liabilities, a shortening of the maturity of liabilities, counterparties asking for more collateral, and negative publicity.

**Exam trap.** Two of the five statements have the right variable with the wrong direction. Check the direction word in each: widening, not narrowing; shortening, not lengthening.
